  - Cast iron bodies, flanged: consistent with CL125B or CL250B per ASME B16.1
  - Steel and stainless steel bodies, flanged: consistent with CL150, 300 and 600 per ASME B16.34
  - Steel and stainless steel bodies, screwed or welding: consistent with flanged CL600 per ASME B16.34
  - These apply "as listed below, unless limited by maximum pressure drop or material temperature capabilities" [p. 3]

- **Pressure ratings for steel valve body, raised-face** (Table on p. 5) [p. 5]:
  - ET: PN16, PN25, PN40, PN63, PN100
  - EAT: PN16, PN25, PN40, PN63, PN100
  - ETR: PN16, PN25, PN40, PN63, PN100

- **Packing limit**: with ENVIRO-SEAL Graphite ULF packing, the maximum pressure/temperature limit is 1500 psig (104 bar) at 600 °F (316 °C) (Table 2, p. 5) [p. 5]

- **Key rule repeated throughout**: Do not exceed the maximum pressure and temperature for the pressure rating of the body material used, even though the trims shown may have higher capabilities [p. 18, p. 19, p. 26]. Also, no pressure or temperature limits in the bulletin, nor any applicable code limitations, should be exceeded [p. 3–5].

So to find your exact maximum pressure, you need to know your valve's pressure class (e.g. CL150/300/600 or PN16–PN100) and body material, then apply the corresponding ASME/EN rating — the datasheet references those standards rather than listing every pressure/temperature pair in these facts.
